annotations.text:
A · ANSWER FIRST — anchored
Proof before commitment: a worked sample is on screen before you type anything, and the 3D stops being the price of entry. Closest of the five to shipping from the current code.
Tradeoff: a photo hero is still doing the persuading, and a sample invites "but that isn't my building".

B · THE LEDGER — anchored
The result is a page, not a modal, and every assumption sits on it, editable in place. The strongest answer to "why should I believe this number", and naturally linkable.
Tradeoff: cold. No image, no hook — the weakest of the five for a first-time visitor arriving from a social link.

C · CIVIC BULLETIN — stretch
Says the true thing first: you cannot buy this yet, and here is the bill that changes it. Turns a dead end into a reason to come back, and the calculator becomes the personalisation underneath.
Tradeoff: buries the calculator the search traffic came for, and it dates the day the Governor signs.

D · SUN DIAL — stretch
The model becomes the interface. No address, no 600KB download, no six-second wait — the number moves as you turn the dial, and the eight sectors are honest about the 45° snap the code already does.
Tradeoff: a toy until someone enters an address, and the furthest of the five from the current brand.

E · BLOCK MAP — stretch
Answers the question the other four leave open: is my number any good? Leads with the city, and comparison is the thing people actually share.
Tradeoff: much the largest build — it needs precomputed figures for every block before the page can render at all.
The one change everything else follows from: the number arrives BEFORE the 3D, not after it. PLUTO alone (floors, height, footprint) is enough to answer in about a second.

Clickable. Press Calculate, then change the facing and floor — the number, the band, the chart and the payback all move live. "Show me the shadows" is a button, not a gate.
Figures come from the real model in js/solar-api.js: $0.34/kWh SC-1, 3% escalation, 0.5% degradation, $1,200 mid-tier kit.
